english.note: Use 叻 as the all-purpose casual adjective for someone who is clever, socially capable, or generally book-smart.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for being capable, skillful, or generally clever.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for a person who is generally capable or skillful.
Use this when capable emphasizes being clever or skilled at something.
Use this when emphasizing that someone is skilful or clever rather than merely adequate.
Choose 叻 when brilliant means especially intelligent, capable, or talented.
Use this when apt means capable or quick to learn, especially when describing a person.
Use this mainly for a person who is skilled, capable, or effective at a task.
Use this for someone who is clever, skilled, or generally capable rather than merely permitted to act.

examples.english: You’re so smart, you finished your homework so quickly.
examples.traditional: 你咁叻，份功課咁快就做完喇。
